text.en: Raju saw a farmer ripening bananas with a gas. "A plant hormone, ethylene!" said his teacher.

Hormones are chemical messengers made in small amounts. Plant hormones include auxins, which cause cell elongation; cytokinins, which promote cell division; gibberellins, which help stem growth; abscisic acid, which helps regulate dormancy and water stress; and ethylene, which promotes ripening in many fruits.
In humans, hormones are made by the endocrine glands, which pour them directly into the blood. The pituitary regulates several other glands and also receives signals from the hypothalamus. The thyroid makes thyroxine, the parathyroid controls calcium, the pancreas makes insulin, the adrenal makes adrenaline and the gonads make sex hormones, while the thymus helps immunity.
Hormones must be balanced. Diabetes can involve too little insulin production, reduced response to insulin, or both. Iodine deficiency can affect thyroid hormone production and is one cause of goitre.
Hormones are chemical messengers made in small amounts.

Plant hormones include auxins that influence cell elongation, cytokinins that promote cell division, gibberellins that influence growth and germination, and abscisic acid that helps regulate dormancy and water stress. Ethylene promotes ripening in many fruits.
In humans, hormones are made by the endocrine glands, which pour them directly into the blood.
The pituitary releases hormones that regulate several other endocrine glands. It also receives signals from the hypothalamus.
The thyroid makes thyroxine, the parathyroid controls calcium, the pancreas makes insulin, the adrenal makes adrenaline and the gonads make sex hormones, while the thymus helps immunity.
Hormones must be balanced.
Diabetes involves high blood glucose when the body makes too little insulin or does not respond to it properly. Iodine deficiency can affect the thyroid and is one cause of goitre.
A hormone carries information from the cells that release it to other cells. A small amount can change how a target tissue works.
A hormone may travel past many cells. Cells with suitable receptors can detect the signal and respond.
Plants have no endocrine glands like those of humans. Some plant cells produce signals that act nearby or travel to other plant parts.
In a young shoot, auxin affects how much cells lengthen. One side can grow faster than the other when light comes from one direction.
The shaded side of a young shoot often lengthens more than the lit side. As the sides grow at different rates, the shoot bends toward the light.

board.text: Unequal growth bends a shoot toward light

text.en: Gibberellins can help a seed begin growing and can also promote stem elongation. The effect depends on the plant and its stage.
Cell division increases the number of cells. Cytokinins help regulate this process in growing tissues.
When water is scarce, abscisic acid can help stomata close. Closing them can reduce further water loss.

board.text: Abscisic acid helps plants respond to dry conditions

text.en: Ethylene is a plant hormone in gas form. It helps coordinate ripening in many fruits, including bananas.

board.text: Ethylene can travel as a gas

text.en: Endocrine cells release their hormones into fluid around the cells, and those hormones enter the blood. Endocrine glands do not need ducts.

board.text: Endocrine glands release signals into blood

text.en: Salivary glands release saliva into ducts leading to the mouth. That differs from hormone release into the blood.
Some pituitary hormones affect growth or water balance. Others help control organs such as the thyroid and adrenal cortex.
Thyroxine helps influence how the body uses energy. Iodine is a material the thyroid needs to make thyroid hormones.

board.text: Thyroid hormones affect the rate of body processes

text.en: The parathyroid glands help control calcium levels in blood. Calcium contributes to functions including muscle activity.
After a meal, rising blood glucose can stimulate insulin release. Insulin helps cells take up glucose and helps the body store some of it.

board.text: The pancreas helps regulate blood glucose

text.en: When blood glucose falls, glucagon can signal the liver to release glucose. It helps keep the supply available between meals.
When insulin helps lower high blood glucose, the original stimulus for insulin release becomes smaller. This is an example of negative feedback.

board.text: Feedback means the response affects the original change

text.en: During sudden alarm, adrenaline can increase heart rate and help prepare the body for quick action. It is released by part of the adrenal gland.
These organs produce hormones involved in puberty and reproduction. Hormone signals help coordinate changes as the body develops.
The thymus helps some immune cells mature. Its role is especially important early in life.
The body adjusts hormone release when conditions change, such as after a meal or between meals. Useful regulation keeps conditions within a working range.

board.text: Hormone levels are regulated, not fixed

text.en: Blood glucose can stay high when little insulin is available, or when cells respond poorly to it. Those are different mechanisms.

board.text: Different problems can affect the same system

text.en: For any example, name the hormone, identify where it acts and describe what changes. This links the messenger to its effect.

problem.en: Which plant hormone promotes ripening in fruits such as bananas?

text.en: It is a plant hormone.
It is a gas.
Ethylene.

problem.en: A young shoot on a windowsill bends towards the window. What makes the bend?

text.en: Cells on the shaded side of the shoot often lengthen more.

why.en: Auxin can influence growth differently on the two sides.

text.en: Unequal elongation curves the shoot towards the brighter side.

why.en: The bend comes from growth rather than the whole shoot turning as one piece.

problem.en: Blood glucose rises after a meal. What hormone response helps bring it down?

text.en: The pancreas can release more insulin.

why.en: Rising blood glucose is the initial stimulus.

text.en: Insulin helps cells take up and store glucose, so blood glucose moves back towards its usual range.

why.en: As glucose falls, the stimulus for more insulin release becomes smaller.

problem.en: Why can a hormone in the blood affect one tissue more than another?

text.en: Target cells have a receptor able to detect the hormone.

why.en: The hormone can travel through the bloodstream without affecting every cell equally.

text.en: Cells that can receive the signal can respond in a way suited to their role.

why.en: A matching receptor is an important part of the response.

prompt.en: A friend says The pancreas makes thyroxine. How will you reply?

The pituitary regulates several other glands and receives signals from the hypothalamus.
